summary:
Walk both sorted lists together. Compare `a[i]` with `b[j]` and record the difference; then advance the pointer
at the smaller value, since moving the larger one could only make the gap wider. O(n + m).

question.md:
Pick one value from each sorted list to minimise `|a[i] − b[j]|`. Return that minimum.

- **Values up to ±10⁹**: differences reach 2 × 10⁹, which still fits a signed 32-bit result but should be
  computed in 64 bits.
- **Up to 10⁵ values each.**

think.md:
`a = [1, 7, 15, 30]`, `b = [4, 12, 19, 28, 40]`. The closest pair is 30 and 28: **2**.

Suppose `a[i] < b[j]`. Pairing `b[j]` with any later `b` value only moves further from `a[i]`, so `a[i]` has
already met its best partner on this side; the only way to find a closer pair is to raise `a[i]`. So advance
the smaller one, exactly like merging.

idea.md: Compute `|a[i] − b[j]|` for all pairs; keep the minimum.

lines.text: Every pair's distance, in 64 bits; the smallest fits in an `int`.

walk.title: Compare every value of a with every value of b.

limits.md: Ignores that both lists are sorted. For each value only its neighbours in the other list matter, which binary search or a merge-style walk finds.

idea.md: For each `x` in `a`, find the first `b[p] ≥ x`; the closest value in `b` is `b[p]` or `b[p − 1]`.

lines.text: Any pair gives a starting answer.
Where `x` would sit in `b`: the first `b[p] ≥ x`.
The closest `b` value is just above (`b[p]`) or just below (`b[p − 1]`) that spot.

steps.text: 1 would go at position 0 in b: check [4]. Best so far 3.
7 would go at position 1 in b: check [4, 12]. Best so far 3.
15 would go at position 2 in b: check [12, 19]. Best so far 3.
30 would go at position 4 in b: check [28, 40]. Best so far 2.

walk.title: For each value in a, binary-search b for where it would go; only the neighbours on either side can be closest.

limits.md: Each search starts from scratch, but as `x` grows its position in `b` only moves right. A single merge-style walk reuses that progress: O(n + m).

idea.md: `i = j = 0`. Record `|a[i] − b[j]|`; advance the pointer at the smaller value. Stop when either list ends.

lines.text: Pointers at the starts; the first pair's gap.
Raise the smaller value: the larger one can only drift further away from it.

steps.text: One list is used up. Smallest difference: 2.

walk.title: Walk both lists together: compare the fronts, then advance the pointer at the smaller value (moving the larger one would only widen the gap).

takeaways.md:
- **Two sorted lists → walk them together**, advancing the smaller side.
- The binary-search version is a good stepping stone and works when one list is much longer.
- Compute differences in 64 bits near the 32-bit limits.
